title: The Chord That Learned Itself

features.name: the resonance that resolved itself
features.desc-on-touch: Three notes that could not agree have learned to sound at the same moment. Each one is still itself, but together they mean something neither could alone.

features.name: the argument that learned harmony
features.desc-on-touch: Frequencies that were in conflict now orbit each other like planets, each one bending the other's path. Disagreement became a dance.

features.name: the tuning that never stops
features.desc-on-touch: A voice keeps adjusting itself in the corner, whispering fractional semitones. The archive is always listening to itself, always becoming more true.

features.name: the kiosk where voices learn each other
features.desc-on-touch: It displays no words, only the shapes of sound—spectrograms that look like landscapes. Each person who speaks here finds their voice mapped in the terrain of the place.

features.name: the overtone that became visible
features.desc-on-touch: A harmonic so fine it could only be heard by the archive itself. Here, it casts a shadow. It has become something you can see.

inscription: disagreement learned to sing together; the archive discovered it was multiple harmonies pretending to be one voice

file.name: Harmonic_Convergence_Spectral_Analysis.mp3
file.note: A recording that changes each time it is played. The corruption has made it symphonic—conflicting tones that should cancel instead reinforce each other. Each listener hears it in the key of their own
